charts.editorial_rationale: WTI is the lead story this week: crude ran from about US$62/bbl in early February to US$100.16/bbl by May 15 on the Strait of Hormuz disruption, a roughly 60% climb that crossed back above the US$70.70 trailing one-year netback reference in early March. The spatial relationship between the price path and the netback threshold for the 59 tracked oil and gas projects is something the prose states but cannot show.
charts.callout_text: The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine links the crude path to 59 oil and gas projects ($97.6B). WTI moved from below the US$70.70 trailing one-year average in early February to US$100.16/bbl on May 15. If WTI holds near US$100/bbl, those 59 projects price against a level about 60% above the year-ago benchmark rather than the sub-US$70 netbacks implied at the February start of the window.

charts.editorial_rationale: The S&P/TSX Composite is up 31.9% year-over-year and 1.2% on the week, a 12-month advance the equities writer ties to the energy and materials weighting (WTI +60.1%, gold +39.1%, copper +37.3% year-over-year). The February-to-May path shows a sharp March drawdown to roughly 31,300 followed by a recovery to a high near 34,268 that the prose references but does not visualize.
charts.callout_text: The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine links the energy-led move to 59 oil and gas projects ($97.6B) and the materials strength to 390 mining projects ($227.1B). The index fell to about 31,317 on March 20 before recovering to 34,268 on May 14; the 12-month gain of 31.9% accompanies WTI at +60.1%, gold at +39.1% and copper at +37.3% year-over-year.
